items.stem: An account falls 25% in a drawdown. Approximately what percentage gain on the remaining balance is needed to get back to even?

options.rationale: Correct: losing 25% leaves 75%, and 0.25/0.75 is about 33%, so a larger gain is needed to recover.
Recovery requires more than the percentage lost because the base is smaller.
That understates the required recovery after a 25% loss.
75% is the remaining balance, not the gain needed.

items.stem: Which TWO inputs are needed to size a position to a fixed dollar risk? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The dollar amount the trader is willing to lose on the trade
options.rationale: Correct: the risk budget is a required input.

options.text: The distance in price from entry to the protective stop
options.rationale: Correct: stop distance determines loss per unit and thus size.

options.text: The all-time high of the market
options.rationale: A historical high does not determine position size.
Account identifiers are irrelevant to sizing.

items.explanation: Correct: the risk budget is a required input.

items.stem: Two open positions are in highly correlated instruments, each risking 1%. Why is the combined risk greater than two independent 1% risks?

options.text: Correlated positions tend to lose together, so their risks add up rather than offset
options.rationale: Correct: positive correlation means the losses are likely to occur at the same time.
Positive correlation increases, not halves, concurrent risk.

options.text: Each position automatically hedges the other
options.rationale: Hedging requires negative correlation, not positive.

options.text: Correlation has no effect on portfolio risk
options.rationale: Correlation is central to portfolio-level risk.

items.explanation: Correct: positive correlation means the losses are likely to occur at the same time.
